title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: custom engine agents for GCC High users
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap's launched status and distinguishes it from the gaps and conflicting statements in Microsoft Learn. Its licensing, limitations and general blocking controls are supported, with GCC High applicability appropriately qualified.

claims.claim: Builder-operated hosting and model consumption are separate direct service costs.
claims.quote: Packaging a capability doesn't remove the cost of operating its dependencies. Include hosting, model usage, storage, networking, credentials, monitoring, and support for any remote MCP servers, APIs, or other services your plugin uses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the researched Learn pages names a separate licence or meter specific to this GCC High release.
claims.quote: Searched: custom engine agents GCC High GCCH licensing price meter release. Read roadmap, prerequisites, FAQ, cost-considerations, overview and Copilot Studio government licensing; none names a licence or meter unique to roadmap item 503771.

claims.claim: The extensibility FAQ says Teams SDK custom engine agent costs depend on the Azure services consumed in the app.
claims.quote: You don't need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license to build custom engine agents by using Teams SDK. Instead, the cost depends on the Azure services consumed in the app.

claims.claim: The extensibility cost page tells custom engine agent builders to budget for their own orchestration, models and hosting.
claims.quote: If you're building a custom engine app or agent, follow the app development path and budget for your own orchestration, models, and hosting.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio US Government licensing is the same as public cloud licensing.
claims.quote: Licensing for Copilot Studio US Government plans is the same as for public cloud.

claims.claim: The known-issues page lists usage billing for extensibility features as unsupported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants.
claims.quote:
The following features aren't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants:
Support for usage billing for extensibility features.

claims.claim: Variable cost reflects potential Azure hosting and service consumption rather than a newly documented GCC High Copilot meter.
claims.quote: Instead, the cost depends on the Azure services consumed in the app.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how this GCC High release's rollout is staged.
claims.quote: Searched: custom engine agents GCC High GCCH enabled default tenant admin switch rollout. Read roadmap, overview, prerequisites, known-issues, service description and government availability table; no release-specific rollout stages were found.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents are supported in app manifest version 1.21 and later.
claims.quote: Custom engine agents are supported in app manifest version 1.21 and later versions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The general agent block path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
select Block or Unblock.
select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The general admin center block action restricts access to the selected agent for the entire organisation.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Blocking Copilot Studio or Agent Builder agents affects Microsoft Copilot and other host products such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agents affects only their availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The lifecycle actions page says GCC High and GCC Moderate support publishing agents to the organisation.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 for government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Government Community Cloud Moderate (GCCM) environments support publishing agents to the organization.
